$doc: Vyomi capability registry — GCP Vertex AI (Gemini publisher models over the local-LLM seam). Proven by tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py.

gcp.vertex-ai.gemini.title: Gemini generateContent / countTokens / streamGenerateContent
limitations: One small local model answers every Gemini model id (llama.cpp on the mesh/appliance, WebLLM on Nano when the page registers one), so quality is toy-grade; with no model running the API returns 503 UNAVAILABLE rather than an answer. Text parts, function calling (functionDeclarations, automatic function calling via google-genai) and responseSchema JSON output work; images/audio/video, Google Search / Vertex AI Search / external-API grounding, code execution, safety settings and tuning are rejected. generateContent with tools[].retrieval.vertexRagStore (a Vertex RAG corpus) runs the retrieval against the corpus first, injects the retrieved chunks into the model's system instruction and returns groundingMetadata (groundingChunks, groundingSupports, retrievalQueries; supports are a lexical overlap match of each answer sentence to the chunks, not Google's attribution model); an unknown corpus is a 404 before any model call. Not attached to streamGenerateContent chunks. modelArmorConfig (promptTemplateName / responseTemplateName, snake or camel case) is honoured: the prompt is sanitized with the stored Model Armor template before the model runs, and a match answers 200 with promptFeedback.blockReason=MODEL_ARMOR + blockReasonMessage and no candidates (model never called; streamGenerateContent too); the answer is sanitized with the response template and a match returns the candidate with finishReason SAFETY and no parts (unary only, not streamed answers). An unknown template is 404, a malformed name 400. Detection is the toy-grade Model Armor engine.

gcp.vertex-ai.embeddings.title: Text embeddings (embedContent / predict)
limitations: Embeddings come from the local embedding model when the backend has one; otherwise from vyomi-hash-embed, a deterministic bag-of-words embedding that is stable and cosine-comparable but not semantic. Dimensions are 256, not the real models' 768/3072.

gcp.vertex-ai.model-garden.title: Model Garden (publisher model catalog: list, get, filter)
limitations: A small fixed catalog of Google, Meta, Mistral and partner models. Only Gemini and text-embedding models can be called (local-LLM seam); other models are catalog entries, and 'Deploy' registers a model + endpoint record without a serving container. publishers/google/models/<id> answers for every id the simulator serves, including the legacy gemini-* / text-embedding-* ids (resolved onto a local catalogue model, said so in vyomiAlias), with version, inputTokenLimit / outputTokenLimit (8192, the local models' window, not Gemini's) and supportedGenerationMethods; google-genai models.get / list work on both the Vertex and Developer-API surfaces.

gcp.vertex-ai.endpoints.title: Endpoints (create, list, get, delete, deployModel, undeployModel, traffic split)
limitations: Deployed models are recorded and shown with their traffic split, but no container serves them: custom-model :predict / :rawPredict answer 501 UNIMPLEMENTED. The exceptions are models Vyomi trained itself (heads and tuned chat models) and imported chat models (LoRA adapter on a SmolLM2 base), which answer :predict and :generateContent. Autoscaling and private endpoints are config-only.

gcp.vertex-ai.models.title: Model Registry (upload, list, get, delete, link to endpoints)
limitations: Model records: artifacts are not validated, versions/aliases and model evaluation are not simulated, models:copy and export answer 501. The exception is a models:upload whose artifactUri (gs://bucket/dir/) holds adapter.gguf and adapter_meta.json (label vyomi-import=chat-lora): it is validated (GGUF header, rank, hidden size, base) and imported as a chat model, a SmolLM2 135M or 360M base plus your LoRA adapter, servable in the Nano console tab only (Mesh and offline keep the record but cannot serve it).

gcp.vertex-ai.datasets.title: Datasets (create, list, get, delete)
limitations: Dataset records only: no data items, annotations, import or export are stored.

gcp.vertex-ai.jobs.title: Training pipelines, custom jobs, batch predictions, hyperparameter tuning, pipeline jobs, tuning jobs (create, list, get, cancel, delete)
limitations: Jobs advance PENDING -> RUNNING -> SUCCEEDED on a clock (about 5 seconds) and never run user containers or produce logs/metrics. A succeeded training pipeline registers its modelToUpload in the Model Registry; batch jobs report an output directory but write no predictions.

gcp.vertex-ai.notebooks.title: Workbench instances (notebooks v2) and Colab Enterprise runtimes/templates (create, list, get, start, stop, delete)
limitations: Control-plane records only: no JupyterLab server or VM is started and the proxy URI does not open a notebook.

gcp.vertex-ai.vector-search.title: Vector Search (indexes, index endpoints, deployIndex, upsert/removeDatapoints, findNeighbors)
limitations: Exact brute-force nearest neighbour over the stored datapoints (cosine, dot-product, L1, squared-L2); no ANN tuning, restricts/filters, sparse embeddings or batch index builds from GCS.

gcp.vertex-ai.feature-store.title: Feature Store (feature groups, features, online stores, feature views)
limitations: Registry records only: no BigQuery sync, feature serving or online lookups.

gcp.vertex-ai.experiments.title: Experiments and metadata (metadata store contexts/artifacts/executions, TensorBoard instances/experiments/runs)
limitations: Records created through the API or console; no experiment tracking SDK run logging, time series or lineage graph.

gcp.gemini-developer-api.title: Gemini Developer API (generativelanguage.googleapis.com, API key) - Dev Simplified alias
limitations: Alias of the Vertex Gemini lane for google-genai / REST clients pointed at base_url with an API key: /v1beta|/v1 models list/get, generateContent, streamGenerateContent (alt=sse), countTokens, embedContent, batchEmbedContents. A missing key returns 403 PERMISSION_DENIED; the key itself is not validated. Same model, limits and rejected features as the Vertex Gemini lane; no Files API, caching, Live API, tuning or Imagen/Veo.

gcp.vertex-ai.agent-engine.title: Agent Engine (reasoningEngines create/get/list/update/delete, :query, :streamQuery) - Vyomi agent spec, Dev Simplified
limitations: Source packages run: vertexai.Client().agent_engines.create(config={source_packages, entrypoint_module, entrypoint_object, class_methods, env_vars}) is stored (spec.sourceCodeSpec.inlineSource archive held server-side, not echoed; responses validate in the SDK, snake_case spec accepted) and :query / :streamQuery run the user's own code: the entrypoint object (instance, or a class that is instantiated) gets set_up() then the registered class method with the request input as keyword arguments, inside the same sandboxed subprocess as Cloud Run functions (metadata-server identity so google.auth.default() works, network allow-list to the simulator, filesystem confinement, deploy-time env_vars + GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT / VYOMI_ENDPOINT / STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST), so the hosted agent can call the simulator with the real Google SDKs. Limits: one fresh process per call (set_up runs each call, no instance state between calls - use sessions / memory), generators are buffered then streamed, requirements.txt is not pip-installed (the pre-baked wheel set is used; a missing package surfaces as the agent's ImportError), the sandbox is a guard-rail not a VM, and Nano (no subprocess) answers FAILED_PRECONDITION for source-packaged engines. Pickled objects (create(agent=<python object>), spec.packageSpec) are stored but never unpickled: :query answers FAILED_PRECONDITION naming the supported form. The Vyomi-spec path is the other way to run an agent: the agent is a Vyomi agent spec (JSON instructions + declarative tools: static/template/builtin calculator/webhook/in-process function) carried in spec.vyomiAgentSpec (REST) or a spec.deploymentSpec.env entry VYOMI_AGENT_SPEC (typed google-cloud-aiplatform gapic clients, transport='rest'), executed as a tool-calling loop over the local model (llama.cpp on the mesh/appliance, WebLLM on Nano). Class methods query, stream_query/async_stream_query and session helpers (create/get/list/delete_session, multi-turn history) are served; :streamQuery events follow the ADK Event shape inside the REST JSON-array-of-HttpBody framing. vertexai.agent_engines.create(<python object>) (cloudpickle + GCS staging), packageSpec/containerSpec deployment, Memory Bank, Example Store and ADK/LangChain/LangGraph runtimes are not supported; an engine with no spec answers :query with FAILED_PRECONDITION, and no model running returns 503 UNAVAILABLE (never a canned answer). Toy-grade quality; webhook tools need network egress (not in Nano's browser); on Nano the loop re-runs after each model await, so keep tools idempotent. gcloud has no reasoning-engines surface in the stable track - use the SDK or REST. State is in the persisted account bag.

gcp.vertex-ai.rag-engine.title: RAG Engine (ragCorpora, ragFiles upload / import from Cloud Storage, retrieveContexts)
limitations: Files arrive by ragFiles:upload (JSON text, base64 content, or the real multipart/related and multipart/form-data bodies) or ragFiles:import from the simulated Cloud Storage (gcsSource.uris: an object or a prefix; unchanged objects are skipped, changed ones re-imported in place). Text, Markdown, CSV, HTML, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX and text-layer PDF are parsed (pure Python, no layout/OCR parsing; legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt fail per file). Chunks are embedded with the local embedding seam (MiniLM in the browser, nomic on the Mesh; a labelled hash embedder when no model runs) and retrieved by exact cosine kNN (no HNSW); ragRetrievalConfig supports topK, hybridSearch.alpha (weighted rank fusion with BM25; alpha 0 = sparse only), vectorDistanceThreshold / vectorSimilarityThreshold and ranking (rerank = embedding + lexical blend, not Google's rank service). Drive, Slack, Jira and SharePoint sources, Spanner / Pinecone / Weaviate / Vertex Vector Search backends and metadata filters are not supported.

gcp.vertex-ai.search.title: Vertex AI Search (data stores, documents import, engines, servingConfigs:search, generated summary)
limitations: Documents come in inline, or from the simulated Cloud Storage (gcsSource.inputUris with dataSchema content, custom or document; BigQuery, Spanner, Firestore and Cloud SQL imports are rejected). Search ranks by hybrid BM25 + embedding reciprocal rank fusion (semantic candidates need cosine >= 0.3); there is no filter / facet / boost / spell-correction spec and no Google semantic ranker. contentSearchSpec.summarySpec returns a generated, cited summary (summaryWithMetadata.citationMetadata) from the small local chat model (not Gemini); with no model running the response carries summarySkippedReasons LLM_ADDON_NOT_ENABLED instead of failing the search.

gcp.vertex-ai.model-armor.title: Security: Model Armor templates and sanitizeUserPrompt / sanitizeModelResponse
limitations: Templates (RAI filters, prompt-injection and jailbreak, basic sensitive-data protection) are really evaluated by the Bedrock Guardrails engine (keyword + local-embedding scoring, regex PII), so detection is toy-grade, not Google's models. Malicious-URI detection (Safe Browsing) and advanced SDP (Cloud DLP templates) are reported EXECUTION_SKIPPED. No floor settings, no SCC / Cloud Logging findings: the page keeps the last 200 sanitize results of this simulator. Prompt injection applies to user prompts only. Enums are accepted as proto integers (what google-cloud-modelarmor sends, alt=json;enum-encoding=int) or names, and answered in ints when the caller asked for them; an enum left at 0 (UNSPECIFIED) means the field is not set.

gcp.vertex-ai.agent-gateway.title: Gateways and MCP servers (agentGateways, mcpServers registry)
limitations: Google's Agent Gateway / Agent Registry have no public API to model: these resources are Vyomi's own (vyomiExtension) over the AgentCore gateway engine. A gateway is a real MCP endpoint (POST /gateways/{id}/mcp) with NONE or JWT auth; attaching an MCP server creates a real mcpServer target (API-key header supported) and tools are listed and called through it. The backing AgentCore gateway also shows in the AWS console of the same account (prefixed gcp-). Calling external MCP servers needs network: direct on the Mesh, through the allow-listed egress relay on Nano.

gcp.vertex-ai.agent-policies.title: Policies (agentPolicies: Cedar over a gateway)
limitations: Vyomi's own resource over the AgentCore policy engine: a real Cedar policy (cedarpy) decides each gateway tool call (principal = JWT subject, action = <target>___<tool>, context.input = arguments); ENFORCE denies by default, LOG_ONLY allows and audits. Mesh/appliance decide with cedarpy; Nano with the same Cedar Rust core compiled to WebAssembly (cedar-wasm 4.14.0, vendored, parity-tested against cedarpy). If the evaluator fails to load, an ENFORCE gateway denies every call (fail closed). Google's org-level agent policies are not modelled.

gcp.vertex-ai.provisioned-throughput.title: Provisioned Throughput (bookkeeping)
limitations: A record of a model, generative model units and a commitment term. Nothing is reserved, enforced or billed (a local model has no shared capacity). Google exposes no public create API for it, so the path is a Vyomi extension.

gcp.vertex-ai.sessions.title: Agent Platform Sessions (reasoningEngines/ID/sessions, events)
limitations: Sessions are the Agent Engine's own multi-turn history for a Vyomi agent spec (list, create, get, delete, events), kept in the account state of this simulator and replayed to the local small model on each query. There is no separate Vertex AI Session Service and no session TTL or expiry. sessions:appendEvent stores a SessionEvent (author, invocationId, timestamp required; content, actions, eventMetadata, errorCode, errorMessage, rawEvent kept as sent) and events list returns them in timestamp order (timestamp filter supported); events are append-only and not fed back to a Vyomi-spec agent's model history.

gcp.vertex-ai.memory-bank.title: Agent Platform Memory Bank (memories create, list, delete, :retrieve, :generate)
limitations: Memories are stored per Agent Engine and ranked by cosine over the local embedding model (the labelled vyomi-hash-embed fallback when no embedding model runs: stable but not semantic). memories:generate asks the small local chat model to extract facts, so quality is toy-grade and it answers 503 when no chat model is running. Memory TTL, revisions and topic-based extraction settings are not implemented.

gcp.vertex-ai.app-builder.title: Agent Builder apps (discoveryengine engines over data stores)
limitations: An app (engine) is a record that links data stores; it is searched with the same hybrid BM25 + embedding ranking as Vertex AI Search (see its limits: inline or simulated Cloud Storage documents, no Google semantic ranker, summaries from the small local model).

gcp.vertex-ai.evaluation.title: Gen AI evaluation (evaluateInstances, evaluationRuns)
limitations: Metrics are exact match, BLEU and ROUGE computed locally, plus the generation step run on the small local model. There is no model-based autorater (no Gemini judge), no pairwise or rubric metrics, and scores will not match Google's evaluation service.

gcp.vertex-ai.metadata.title: Vertex ML Metadata (metadataStores/default: artifacts, executions, contexts)
limitations: Artifacts, executions and contexts are stored and listed as records in metadataStores/default. There is no lineage graph query and no artifact versioning; Vyomi's own training, pipeline and tuning jobs do not write into the store, so lineage appears only when your code records it.

gcp.vertex-ai.monitoring.title: Model Monitoring (modelDeploymentMonitoringJobs)
limitations: Jobs are created, paused and resumed through their lifecycle (PENDING then RUNNING) and are bound to a deployed endpoint. No drift or skew statistics are computed and no alerts are raised: the job is a record.

gcp.vertex-ai.agent-registry.title: Agent Registry (read view over Agent Engine deployments)
limitations: A read-only list of the agents deployed as reasoningEngines across regions, with the model and tools their Vyomi agent spec declares. Google publishes no registry API, so this is a Vyomi view, not a separate resource: there is no publish, approval or versioning workflow.

gcp.vertex-ai.topology.title: Agent topology (agents, models, tools graph)
limitations: A drawing of agent, model and tool nodes taken from the live Agent Engine specs. It shows declared tools, not runtime call traffic, and Google publishes no topology API, so it is a Vyomi view.

gcp.vertex-ai.adk.title: Agent Development Kit deployment
limitations: Deploying creates an Agent Engine reasoningEngine from a Vyomi agent spec (JSON instructions, model and declarative tools). The Google ADK Python framework and pickled agent classes are not executed.

gcp.vertex-ai.mcp-servers.title: MCP servers (registry of MCP endpoints)
limitations: A catalogue of MCP server records (create, list, delete, listTools); attaching one to a gateway creates a real AgentCore mcpServer target. Google publishes no public API for it, so the path is a Vyomi extension. On Nano, tool calls reach a server only through the egress bridge (a local tunnel or the hosted allow-list relay).
